root.title: Operate, secure and keep safe MMA 2 (73-car Bakken crude train) at Nantes, 5-6 July 2013

children.title: Provide fit equipment and a safe operating framework (organisational, before the event)
Repair and maintain locomotive 5017
Define securement rules and special instructions for parked trains
Approve single-person train operation (SPTO)
Oversee compliance with securement rules (CROR s.112) and safety culture
Operate MMA 2 from Farnham to Nantes (engineer alone)
Assess condition of lead locomotive 5017 and decide to continue
Drive train to crew-change point at Nantes
Park train at Nantes
Select parking location (main line vs. siding with derail)
Stop train on 1.2% grade and apply automatic/independent air brakes
Secure train against movement
Determine number of hand brakes required
Apply hand brakes
Test hand-brake effectiveness (air brakes released, train must hold)
Shut down locomotives and secure cab
Report status and hand over
Report train secure to rail traffic controller (RTC) Farnham
Report locomotive 5017 defects (smoke, surges) to RTC Bangor
RTC assesses report and decides on action for defective locomotive
Leave site for hotel and escalate safety concern
Respond to locomotive fire (about 23:50-00:13)
Report fire (911) and dispatch Nantes fire department and police
Shut down engine of 5017 and extinguish fire
Notify MMA RTC and decide on railway follow-up
Verify that train is safe before emergency services leave
Keep unattended train in a safe state (00:13-01:14)
Maintain brake force while air pressure leaks away
Detect movement of unattended train
Stop or warn about runaway train before the town

ttaRecords.comments: Scenario: unattended MMA 2 rolled 11 km from Nantes and derailed in Lac-Mégantic at about 01:14 on 6 July 2013; 47 killed. TSB final report (Aug 2014) identified 18 causes and contributing factors. Data compiled from the Wikipedia article on the disaster; human error classification is the analyst's interpretation, not a TSB finding.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Non-standard repair (epoxy-like material) used instead of proper engine repair
ttaRecords.recovery: Post-repair inspection; locomotive inspection regime; crews reporting defects
ttaRecords.consequence: Repair fails in service: engine surges, black/white smoke, oil collects in turbocharger and ignites on the night of the accident
psf: Cost and time pressure to return locomotive to service
ttaRecords.comments: Repaired October 2012 after engine failure. TSB found years of deferred maintenance on 5017 and on five other inspected locomotives.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Special instructions require too few hand brakes and give no grade-dependent guidance
ttaRecords.recovery: Regulator validation of special instructions (none performed); company risk assessment
ttaRecords.consequence: Crew following procedure under-secures train on 1.2% grade (9 brakes per MMA procedure vs. 17-26 needed per TSB)
ttaRecords.comments: Transport Canada does not validate railways' special instructions or specify number of brakes. Sources differ on MMA's stated requirement (9 brakes per TSB/charges; 5 locomotives + 11 cars per MMA claim).

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Single-person operation allowed without the public permit process; no second crew member
ttaRecords.recovery: Second person could have performed stabilisation test or checked securement
ttaRecords.consequence: No independent check of securement or brake test; no ground person
ttaRecords.comments: Average of about 80 tank cars per train under one person. TSB could not conclude whether a second crew member would have prevented the accident.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Repeated CROR s.112 hand-brake violations at Nantes met only by reprimands, no fines
ttaRecords.recovery: Regulator inspection; company audit and supervision
ttaRecords.consequence: Non-compliant securement practice normalised; no corrective barrier before the accident
ttaRecords.comments: Reprimands 2004-2009, 2011 and 2012. Auditor General (2011) found weak follow-up by Transport Canada. No rule prohibited leaving an unattended train on the main line.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Defective locomotive continued in service despite abnormal smoke and engine surges
ttaRecords.recovery: Report to RTC; locomotive swap; stop and wait for repair
ttaRecords.consequence: Train with known-defective lead locomotive arrives at Nantes; fire risk while unattended
ttaRecords.comments: Engineer told the RTC that the locomotive had mechanical difficulties throughout the trip.
Train stopped at about 23:00 at the designated crew-change point at Nantes, 11 km west of Lac-Mégantic.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Train parked on main line instead of siding with derail
ttaRecords.recovery: Siding with derail; alternative crew-change location
ttaRecords.consequence: Loaded train unattended on main line above town with no physical barrier against runaway
psf: Infrastructure / layout (siding used to store Tafisa boxcars)
ttaRecords.comments: TSB: MMA operating plan was to leave the train on the main line, unattended, cab unlocked, next to a public highway. Transport Canada called it unusual, but no regulation prohibited it.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Brake holding relied on air system that depends on a running compressor
ttaRecords.recovery: Hand brakes; keeping a locomotive running to feed the compressor
ttaRecords.consequence: Air-brake effectiveness decays as air leaks once compressors stop
ttaRecords.comments: Slow, steady leakage does not trigger automatic brake application.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Too few hand brakes judged sufficient
ttaRecords.recovery: Hand-brake test; RTC check of hand-brake count (not required at the time)
ttaRecords.consequence: Seven hand brakes applied vs. 17-26 needed (TSB); none on the 72 tank cars
ttaRecords.comments: Reports differ: an MMA board member claimed 5 locomotives and 10 cars; TSB agrees with the engineer's statement (5 locomotives, buffer car, remote-control car).

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Hand brakes applied on too few vehicles and with variable force
ttaRecords.recovery: Retarding force check via push/pull test; second person to verify
ttaRecords.consequence: Train held only by air brakes plus a few hand brakes
ttaRecords.comments: Hand-brake effectiveness depends on age, maintenance and the force exerted by the person applying it.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Hand-brake test performed with locomotive air brakes still applied
ttaRecords.recovery: Second person performing the test; releasing all air brakes and checking that the train holds
ttaRecords.consequence: False confidence that hand brakes alone would hold the train
ttaRecords.comments: CROR s.112 requires hand-brake effectiveness to be tested. In the second trial the engineer was convicted under railway safety legislation for not testing the hand brakes; the 2018 criminal negligence trial ended in acquittal.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Four of five locomotives shut down; 5017 left running, cab unlocked, reverser not removed
ttaRecords.recovery: Locked cab and removed reverser (required only after July 2013 emergency directive)
ttaRecords.consequence: Defective engine left running unattended; later shutdown by third parties removes air supply to brakes
ttaRecords.comments: TSB: reset safety control on 5017 was not wired to apply the whole train's brakes on engine failure.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Train reported secure without independent verification of securement
ttaRecords.recovery: RTC requests hand-brake count and grade (not required at the time)
ttaRecords.consequence: RTC holds a false picture of train securement
ttaRecords.comments: The FRA emergency order of 2 August 2013 later required notification of hand-brake count, train length, grade and weather before leaving a train unattended.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Defect reported but fire risk and unattended running not escalated or risk-assessed
ttaRecords.recovery: RTC orders repair, locomotive swap or keeps crew on site
ttaRecords.consequence: Parties agree to deal with the smoking locomotive the next morning; defective engine runs unattended overnight
ttaRecords.comments: Report made to the RTC in Bangor, Maine.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: No action required on defective locomotive that night
ttaRecords.recovery: Management escalation; locomotive removal from service
ttaRecords.consequence: No barrier against locomotive fire while the train is unattended
ttaRecords.comments: TSB identified a lack of backup safety mechanisms and several failures of training and oversight.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Safety concern voiced but escalation not documented
ttaRecords.recovery: Call to MMA US office (Hermon, Maine); remaining on site
ttaRecords.consequence: Train left unattended overnight with running, smoking locomotive
ttaRecords.comments: Engineer told the taxi driver he felt unsafe and wanted to call the US office. Sources reviewed do not state whether the call was made.
A citizen called 911 at 23:50 about a fire on the first locomotive. Nantes fire department and a Sûreté du Québec officer responded.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Engine shut down per fire protocol without awareness of the air-brake consequence
ttaRecords.recovery: Qualified railway employee on site; restart of compressor
ttaRecords.consequence: Compressor stops; air brakes slowly lose effectiveness
ttaRecords.comments: Fire chief: protocol is to shut the engine down to stop fuel feeding the fire. Locomotives that could restart the air brakes automatically were shut down.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Engineer not recalled; track maintenance foreman unfamiliar with air brakes sent instead
ttaRecords.recovery: Recall engineer or other qualified crew; consult brake expert
ttaRecords.consequence: Nobody with air-brake competence re-assessed securement after the engine was shut down
ttaRecords.comments: MMA did not grant permission for the engineer to return to the scene.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Train confirmed safe without testing brakes or checking air pressure
ttaRecords.recovery: Hand-brake test; check of air pressure and hand-brake count
ttaRecords.consequence: Last barrier lost at about 00:13; firefighters leave and the train stays unattended until it starts to roll at 00:56
ttaRecords.comments: Two MMA track maintenance employees arrived by 00:13 and told the police officer and the Farnham RTC that the train was safe.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Air pressure falls until brakes and hand brakes cannot hold the train (00:56)
ttaRecords.recovery: Running compressor (shut down); automatic restart of air-brake system; more hand brakes; derail
ttaRecords.consequence: Train begins to roll towards Lac-Mégantic, 11 km away on a 1.2% grade
ttaRecords.humanErrorType: Latent condition (no active error at this step)
ttaRecords.comments: Nantes siding had a derail that could have prevented accidental departure; it was not used.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: Runaway not detected: no track circuits or other monitoring on the line
ttaRecords.recovery: Track circuits alerting the RTC; witnesses; level-crossing warnings
ttaRecords.consequence: Train accelerates unnoticed down the grade and reaches about 105 km/h, over six times the 16 km/h limit at the yard
ttaRecords.humanErrorType: Latent condition (no active error at this step)
ttaRecords.comments: A firefighter saw the train pass a crossing about ten minutes before the derailment, without lights or horn.

ttaRecords.externalErrorMode: No barrier able to stop or warn about the runaway train
ttaRecords.recovery: None effective
ttaRecords.consequence: Derailment at about 01:14; 63 of 72 tank cars derailed, about 6 million litres of crude released, fire and explosions; 47 killed, more than 30 buildings destroyed
ttaRecords.humanErrorType: Latent condition (no active error at this step)
ttaRecords.comments: Heavy damage also driven by DOT-111 tank cars known for high failure rates in accidents.
